“I’ve detected a long range missile heading straight for us”. Tao paused almost as if in shock at what she was reading on her HUD. “John.. the signature is giving me a 68% likelihood It’s protectant” She looked up at John in disbelief “Marcellus?” John pulled open his HUD and began reading over what Tao was picking up on her HUD. Beads of sweat ran down Tex’s forehead. Shai Tao and Tex looked back at each other then looked back to John. Almost as if to ask if anyone had a solution  “Does anyone know what the fuck is going on” said Tex. “We’ve got 4 minutes until this place is buried in the mountain” Tao was busy plotting an exit route with the help of Kitten in her wrist terminal. The once silent halls leading up to the conversion chamber they all stood steadfast in now spoke as countless blast doors along the hall rapidly closed shut entombing them deeper within the mountain. John looked back at his Mark IV and began climbing back into its gelatinous mould. Small sparks, not vicious but like a silent glow illuminated around his carapace as he slid into its hold. He was calm and quiet in doing so, like nothing was happening. “I’m locked out of the Dam mainframe!” Tao’s voice echoed back to them in the vast laboratory with intensity, beads of sweat ran down her forehead. Shai quivered in her suit, she felt her hairs tense as goosebumps ran down her spine, then she tracked John walking across the room to the blast door in his Mark IV.

John placed his hand on the blast door, but this time instead of forcing the seams apart, he just rested it there as though to be listening. He ejected his suit’s interface chord and plugged into the terminal at the wall next to it, the tentacle-like coils reaching out like sniffers found their connection’s almost intuitively. “Give me a second”. John felt himself flowing through the facility once more. He closed his eyes and found himself transgressing the walls, flying through a grid marking nodes on each blast door as he raced through the illuminated route Tao had planned. He could see himself and his allies in the room, the others eagerly looking on at him as he stood against the blast door like a statue in a sleep-like state. Then, it was done. The blast door jolted open and John stepped out easing into a run. The others all looked at each other, Then they fell in formation behind him. Tex at the back shrugged his shoulders and followed.

“Seems like you’ve done this before cap” Tex felt uneasy by John’s sudden newfound familiarity with the facility. “Yeah I don’t know” John didn’t seem bothered by the steady run along the route Tao had planned out, speaking without fault or pause as each upcoming blast door seemed to open in anticipation of his approach. “I feel like I’ve been a part of this facility since it’s fruition, like it’s a part of my body. I seem to be able to speak to her”, “Ooh k chief, understand. Well, at least we know you’re on our side and maybe she’s on our side too”, “It would seem that way, whoever left this place. They either wanted it to land in the right hands or they had a plan in case it landed in the wrong hands” John paused for a moment. “I’m hoping that the latter isn’t the case, and that fucking missile is completely independent of the facilities lock down procedure”.

“On that missile, we’ve got three minutes to get out of here before it becomes our tomb” Tao raised her rifle up siting the deep halls ahead, slowing her pace behind John “John.. the floating Pods are just up ahead”. John seemed unphased by Tao’s statement. “I know” said John, keeping his pace. Tao didn’t know what to expect on the other side or what the Pod’s were there for in the first place. On their rapid descent past the pods they had a short glimpse of the floating structure hanging between the mountains. “One more blast..” John had stopped up ahead, Tao had all but forgotten what she was going to say, slowing her pace arriving just behind John. The others arrived behind her momentarily heaving and coughing catching their breath. John seemed unphased, breathing normally. The sound of grinding steel came to a halt as the final blast door retracted into the mountain, a dim evening light with daggers of cold wind ice and snow pelted them simultaneously, stinging but inviting them out. Their suit’s compensated for the push of the blizzard winds, digging their heels into snow piled atop steel grates that stretched outwards past the mountainous cavern's mouth. Icy winds grasped John as he walked slowly toward the cavern mouth, the others observed the a blanket of ice forming over his suits shoulders as he pushed slowly forward

“Missile Incoming! ETA 1 minute, 30 seconds” strobed on their HUDS. For a moment the Blizzard went silent, opening up the evening night sky. It was all too mesmerising as they looked on, they lost all touch with the gravity of their surroundings. A plethora of colours stars and nebulas stared back at them, so clear. The team took a moment to appreciate the beauty of how far the human race had come. Towering wires suspended a snake-like structure bypassing the saddle of the mountain valley below. The “Pods” Tau had referred to earlier, hung between suspended walkways like nodes from wires reaching up above that shot to the higher ridges of each mountain face, suspending the structure. It was impressive to anyone who had never seen it clearly before. Encapsulated amidst the constant fog of the mountains, the suspended structure extended and weaved following the valley for some time until it turned again, connecting to the face of the cliff on the other side. A silhouette of dark velvet purple flicked with specks of white like waves opening up to blues then bright pinks, they felt their souls riding the stars in another universe, then they were pulled back. “John, this valley is never this clear! they’re beaming our location so the missile can maintain it’s fix!” John observed a slight radiation spike on his HUD then looked ahead at the first Pod and began charging toward it, the others falling in rapidly behind him. “I’ve seen what’s on the other side, it takes us deep into the northernmost mountain. We should be able to seek shelter on the other side within the mountain then make our way down to the saddle” John now panted as the words spilled out from him with haste. There wasn’t any more time to explain. He made it to the first Pod and heard a jilt as the motors seized. The ice on the first Pod’s blast door was so thick that it had locked the blast door closed.

"Fuck, it’s completely frozen over,” John punched the blast door, clenching his teeth in frustration as his jaw grinded to a lock. Nothing happened, but a the slightest crack nuanced the surface of the murky dirt strewn ice that had entombed the pod near on half a century.

He stepped to the side of the floating grate, gripping one of the fixed wire ropes that the structure and his team hung so delicately from in the treacherous wind. John veered over the roof of the pod with determined eyes, gripping the steel rope firmly in his gauntlet. He placed his other hand just above the blast door, then began pulling himself up in an attempt to reach the pod's roof.

The weight distribution of the suit felt awkward. Shards of ice cracked from the rope, his gauntlet sliding down to meet the edging of the grate as his body followed. John felt as though he had begun to fall indefinitely, immersed in another time, falling backwards looking up at the night sky. The valley floor awaited his fragile shell, and he could see the wailing arms of the worker bots that had just been tossed off the bridge as they fell momentarily after him, meeting the same fate in what felt like the end of a bad dream.

As he looked up, he could make out a familiar figure glaring back at him. Blue eyes, cold like steel, the dead glow of night sharpening their glare, gripped his soul. “Captain!” The menacing blue eyes vanished into thin air.

Shai had placed her hand underneath his armpit and began lifting him to his feet from where he had fallen hard on the grate. John came to, finding his gaze fixed on the bottom of the valley below. He could see a misty fog with a subtle blue glow, which he assumed to be some strange reflection of the evening sky, yet peculiar.

“We need to move!” Shouted Shai. John shook his head, disoriented and shocked at the vision he had just seen, then looked to his HUD. “Guess it’s time to put the suit to the test.”

Shai stepped back after lifting John to his feet. She knelt down, lined up the landing DZ on the roof of the Pod from her fly-by scan earlier before they completed their dives. Shai carefully focused with her mind on the directions to move the landing marker on the scan with her neural interface. She managed to select in her mind 3 variables by imagining the numbers. She focused. “10, 4000, 2000”. As she thought of the arrow xyz coordinates, she pinpointed the center of the 1st pod's roof. She imagined herself gliding with the assisted thrusters, easing her down onto the next roof.

“See you 3 over there,” the words escaped her with a shaky confidence as she stirred with thoughts of all the interacting systems that could fail her, as they had with previous suits. She charged back her legs, lowering her center of gravity closer to the ground, ready to pounce.

The sound of high pressure fluid hummed as her hydraulic drive pipes powered up from her suit’s hydrogen combustion engine. High pitched hissing and pops ever so silently eased down as her drive pipes charged. Hydrogen engines were vastly adapted and the newer suits dampening made them again even quieter than their gasoline counterparts.
